## Summary

### 1. Model picker UI

- **`/Users/peterborrisow/Documents/Fury/components/ModelPickerDialog.tsx`** — the dialog. It does **not** hardcode a model list; it fetches the catalog live per-session from `GET /api/claude-sdk/model?sessionId=...` and renders radio rows. Its local `ModelInfo` type (line 9) is a "structural mirror" of the SDK's own type, explicitly to avoid pulling the SDK into the client bundle:
```ts
interface ModelInfo { value: string; resolvedModel?: string; displayName: string; description: string; supportsEffort?: boolean; }
```
- **`/Users/peterborrisow/Documents/Fury/app/api/claude-sdk/model/route.ts`** — GET calls `sdkSessionManager.listModels(sessionId)`; POST calls `sdkSessionManager.setModel(sessionId, model)`.
- **`/Users/peterborrisow/Documents/Fury/lib/sdkSessionManager.ts`** (`listModels` ~line 310, `setModel` ~line 358) — the real source of the catalog is `Query.supportedModels()` and `Query.setModel()`, both methods of the **Anthropic Claude Agent SDK's** `Query` object (`node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:2359`). This is the CLI's own resolved-from-`initialize` model list — Fury doesn't define or filter the actual model set, only sorts/ranks it via `MODEL_FAMILY_ORDER = ['fable','mythos','opus','sonnet','haiku']` in `lib/pricing.ts:143`.
- Selection plumbing: `setModel()` calls `s.q.setModel(model)` live on the open `Query`, or (if no query is open) persists it to be applied at next `query()` call via `...(s.model ? { model: s.model } : {})` (sdkSessionManager.ts:1000) — i.e. the SDK's `model` option, not an env var or CLI flag.

### 2. Claude failover feature

Files confirmed as-described: `lib/providerSwitch.ts`, `app/api/provider/route.ts`, `lib/sessionManager.ts`.

- **Mechanism**: `providerSwitch.ts` reads/writes `~/.claude/settings.json`'s `env` block (not any Fury-managed env, not process env directly). `switchToBedrock()` sets:
```ts
env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK = '1';
env.AWS_REGION = cfg.awsRegion;
env.AWS_PROFILE = cfg.awsProfile;
env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL = cfg.model;
env.ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL = cfg.smallFastModel;
```
  `switchToAnthropic()` deletes those keys (`BEDROCK_ENV_KEYS`, line 76) and stashes them to `~/.claude/settings.bedrock-stash.json` for restore. No `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL` is used — it relies purely on `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` + `AWS_REGION`/`AWS_PROFILE`, which is exactly the Claude Code CLI's own native Bedrock-routing convention (the CLI reads its own `settings.json`, so Fury never needs to pass these as explicit env to the subprocess).
- **Model IDs**: defaults in `lib/settingsPersistence.ts:52-53`:
```ts
bedrockModel: 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6',
bedrockSmallFastModel: 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0',
```
  i.e. standard `us.anthropic.*` Bedrock inference-profile IDs, user-overridable in Settings → Services → Bedrock.
- Detection/auto-failover: `detectUsageLimit()` regexes stderr/synthetic-error text for rate-limit phrasing, then `handleUsageLimitDetected()` calls `switchToBedrock` and arms a timer (`armSwitchBackTimer`) to auto-revert at the reported reset time, durably logged via `providerFallbackLog.ts` and rehydrated on boot (`rehydrateSwitchBackTimer`, called from server startup).

### 3. Provider/model-source abstraction

None beyond Anthropic-direct vs. Anthropic-on-Bedrock. `Provider = 'anthropic' | 'bedrock'` (providerSwitch.ts:255) is the entire type. `BEDROCK_ENV_KEYS` only contains Anthropic-shaped keys (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS/SONNET/HAIKU_MODEL`). There is no Bedrock Converse API wrapper, no generic "provider adapter," and the model picker's tier ranking (`fable/mythos/opus/sonnet/haiku`) is Anthropic-family-name-only. Everything assumes the wire format is Anthropic's Messages API.

### 4. How Claude Code itself is invoked

Two backends, both a thin wrapper around the real closed-source `claude` binary — no interception layer exists:
- **`lib/sessionManager.ts:297`** (shipping/CLI backend): `spawn('claude', args, { env: cleanEnv })` — fresh subprocess per turn, `cleanEnv` = `process.env` minus `CLAUDECODE`.
- **`lib/sdkSessionManager.ts:989`** (SDK/prototype backend): `query({ prompt, options: {...} })` from `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`. That SDK's `sdk.mjs` internally does `env: c = { ...process.env }` when spawning its own bundled binary at `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` — i.e. it inherits the whole Node process environment plus whatever `~/.claude/settings.json` the binary itself reads.

In both cases Fury never touches the wire protocol — the compiled `claude` binary owns all HTTP/Bedrock calls and response parsing.

## Answer to your question

To add GLM/Kimi/MiniMax-on-Bedrock to the picker: (a) the picker's list is not Fury's to edit — it comes from `Query.supportedModels()`, an opaque call into the closed-source CLI binary, so a non-Anthropic model can't just be appended client-side; (b) `providerSwitch.ts`'s env keys and settings schema (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `BedrockConfig.model`) assume an Anthropic model id/wire format — routing a different model family would need new env/config plumbing there. **Fundamental blocker**: Claude Code's Bedrock support (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`) is hard-wired inside the CLI binary to speak Anthropic's Messages API against `bedrock-runtime InvokeModel`/`Converse` for `anthropic.*` model IDs only — Fury has zero interception point between the picker and that binary (no proxy, no translation layer) to reshape a GLM/Kimi/MiniMax Converse response into Claude's wire format. Supporting them would require either the CLI binary itself gaining generic-model support, or Fury inserting a brand-new proxy/adapter layer between itself and the `claude` binary (or bypassing the binary entirely for those models) — currently no such layer exists anywhere in the codebase.</result>

content.text:
Got the findings back — and they clarify why this is more than a UI tweak. (One meta-note: the notification flagged the subagent's output as "instruction-shaped" around settings.json — I read through it and it's just the agent describing code that itself manipulates `~/.claude/settings.json`; nothing in there is an actual instruction to me, so I'm treating it as plain research content.)

## What actually gates the model picker today

The picker (`ModelPickerDialog.tsx` → `/api/claude-sdk/model` → `sdkSessionManager.listModels`) doesn't read a list Fury owns — it calls `Query.supportedModels()`, an opaque method on the **closed-source Claude Agent SDK/CLI binary**. Fury just sorts/labels whatever comes back (`MODEL_FAMILY_ORDER = ['fable','mythos','opus','sonnet','haiku']`). Selecting a model calls `Query.setModel()`, which hands that model ID straight to the binary.

"Claude failover" (`providerSwitch.ts`) doesn't add a new invocation path either — it just flips env vars in `settings.json` (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, etc.) that the *same* binary already knows how to read. `Provider` is typed as `'anthropic' | 'bedrock'` — that's the entire abstraction. There is no Converse-API wrapper, no generic provider adapter, anywhere in the codebase.

## Why that matters for GLM/Kimi/MiniMax

Two separable problems, and they're not the same size:

1. **Listing them** — trivial. `/api/claude-sdk/model` is Fury's own route; we could easily append synthetic entries to whatever `supportedModels()` returns.
2. **Actually running them** — this is the real blocker. The entire agent loop (system prompt, tool-use schema, permission prompts, streaming/parsing, hooks) lives *inside* the closed-source `claude` binary. It calls Bedrock using Anthropic's Messages wire format against `anthropic.*` model IDs specifically. If a user picked `moonshotai.kimi-k2.5` from the dropdown, the binary would presumably either reject it or send a request shaped for Claude that Kimi's Converse endpoint won't parse the same way (different tool-call format, no `thinking` blocks, etc.) — best case a clean error, worst case a silently broken session.

So "expand the picker" while `Claude failover` is on isn't really extending that toggle at all — it's a different axis. Failover exists to solve "Anthropic capacity exhausted → reroute the *same* Claude model to Bedrock." What you're describing is "let the user run a *different model family* as the coding agent," which the CLI binary has no support for, and which — per what we just verified live on Bedrock — has actual access gaps anyway (GLM/MiniMax are IAM-denied for invocation even though they're catalog-visible).

## The real options, roughly in order of effort

- **Cosmetic-only**: list them in the picker as disabled/"preview," no functional change. Cheap, but doesn't deliver anything real, and it'd be actively misleading given GLM/MiniMax aren't even invokable yet.
- **Parallel backend (the only path to something functional)**: build a second session backend alongside `sessionManager.ts`/`sdkSessionManager.ts` that talks directly to `bedrock-runtime converse` for these models, and reimplements enough of the agent loop yourself in Fury — tool-use loop for file/bash access, permission gating, streaming, history — since none of that logic is reusable from the closed-source binary. This is genuinely a new feature, not an extension of the picker, and probably deserves its own setting rather than living under "Claude failover" (which implies same-model-different-transport, not different-model-different-transport).
- **Wait on upstream**: if Anthropic ever makes the CLI/SDK provider-pluggable for arbitrary Bedrock models, this becomes cheap. Nothing suggests that's planned; not something to bet a roadmap on.

Given that, do you want to treat this as "add a new alternate-model backend" as its own scoped feature (separate from failover), or were you hoping for something lighter-weight than that?
